videos.caption: 9 Best Things to Do in Marrakesh 🕌✨ 1) Stay in a Riad 🛏️  feel the authentic Moroccan vibe, from the mosaic tiles to the whisper-quiet courtyards. Riads offer privacy, fewer crowds, and a home-away-from-home feel with traditional decor, often a peaceful rooftop terrace, and staff who treat you like family. Perfect for a truly Moroccan experience without the hotel hustle. 2) Best Coffee at Bacha Coffee ☕️✨ (Location: https://goo.gl/maps/6u3Xx9J9xqv1w9Qw7) Silky espresso, perfectly balanced blends, and a chic, relaxed atmosphere. Great latte art, friendly baristas, and a bright, stylish space to post your vibes. Pro tip: try their signature crush coffee and pastry pairing. 3) Explore the Souks 🧿🌀 Fun tip: haggle with a smile, never agree to the first price! Make it a playful game, sample spices, and test your bargaining skills. Lose yourself in ribbons of color, leather, pottery, and lamps. The thrill of the find is half the fun! 4) Visit Ben Youssef Madrasa 🕌 A jaw-dropping historic site with intricate tilework, carved wood, and serene courtyards. It’s a perfect spot for photos that scream old-world Marrakech charm. 5) Jardin Majorelle 🌿💙 iconic cobalt-blue paths, lush botanical displays, and a peaceful escape from the market buzz. A must-see for color lovers and plant enthusiasts, plus it’s connected to the Yves Saint Laurent legacy. 6) Ourika Valley Day Trip 🚙🌄 about 1 hour from central Marrakech (depending on traffic). What to expect: stunning valley scenery, Berber villages, waterfalls, and a cooler climate. A refreshing break from the medina with photo-worthy viewpoints. 7) Agafay Desert Experience 🐫🏜️ Highlights: camel ride under the open sky, squad  bike moments, and magical desert views. Luxe touch: stay at a desert camp with plush lounges, gourmet meals, and starlit dinners. Perfect for a memorable  outing. 8) Dinner at La Trattoria 🍝🇮🇹  warm, cozy ambiance with authentic Italian flavors in Marrakech. Great for a relaxed evening, fresh pastas, and a lively dining vibe after a day of exploration. 9) Jemaa el-Fnaa - The Heart of Marrakech 🎭💃 Do it for the vibes: bustling square, street performances, snake charmers, and a feast for the senses. Pro tip: bring some cash for photos with performers and for quick bites. Best times: late afternoon into evening when the energy peaks. #Marrakesh #Morocco #TravelTikTok #Riads #Souks

Would you wander Marrakech alone?  One thing I was honestly nervous about before coming to Marrakech for the first time was safety, especially as a woman travelling alone. Social media can make the medina look super intimidating, chaotic, and overwhelming, but my experience has actually been really positive. Of course you need to stay aware like in any big city, but I’ve spent hours wandering the souks, getting lost in little alleyways, shopping, stopping for mint tea, and exploring on my own and I genuinely felt okay. One thing that helped SO much this time was not carrying all my luggage around with me 😅 dragging a huge backpack through crowded streets instantly makes you feel more stressed and overwhelmed. I used @bounce luggage storage so I could explore Marrakech freely for the day before my riad check-in, and it made such a difference. I could actually enjoy the medina instead of worrying about my bags the entire time. Bounce has thousands of locations worldwide and is a super reliable resource if you find yourself in a similar situation as me. From getting around Marrakech to booking attractions, exploring the souks and even travelling with a drone, here are a few things to know before visiting Marrakech 👇🏼 📍 Getting around Marrakech — we found the inDrive app much easier because you can see the price before accepting the ride rather than negotiating with taxis. 🌿 Jardin Majorelle tickets — BOOK IN ADVANCE! This is one of the most popular things to do in Marrakech and tickets can sell out. 🕌 Madrasa Ben Youssef — we bought our tickets when we arrived, so you don’t necessarily need to pre-book this one. 🚁 Bringing a drone to Morocco — drones are restricted in Morocco. As full-time travellers carrying ours onwards, we declared it on arrival and left it with customs to collect again when leaving. 🛍️ Marrakech souks — bargaining is normal, so look around and compare prices before buying. Planning a trip to Morocco? 🇲🇦 SAVE this for later! Here are 7 things you should know before you go: 1️⃣ Haggling & Shopping — Don’t buy the first thing you see. Shop around, compare prices, and negotiate. 2️⃣ Tourist Pricing — Be mindful of how you identify yourself and where you’re from, as tourist prices can be higher. 3️⃣ Be Comfortable Saying NO — If you show interest in something, sellers may really try to make the sale. Be polite, but be firm. 4️⃣ Make Restaurant Reservations — Popular restaurants can book up, so reserve ahead of time if there’s somewhere you really want to visit. 5️⃣ Know How Taxis Work — Understand the pricing and meter system before getting in. 6️⃣ Explore Beyond Marrakech — You can experience a lot of Marrakech in 3–4 days, so use extra time to explore other parts of Morocco. 7️⃣ Agafay ≠ The Sahara — Agafay is beautiful, but it’s not the same as experiencing the iconic Sahara sand dunes. If you have the time, consider an overnight Sahara trip. Morocco is an incredible country, but knowing these things BEFORE you go can make your trip so much smoother. 🇲🇦✨ Save this for your Morocco trip and send it to your travel buddy! ✈️🐪 #traveltips #travelguide #travelcreator #moroccotravel #travelinspiration
